title: Entity
description: An actor in the registry: a campaign, a party, a candidate, a third party spender, a broadcaster or a vendor. Observations and estimates reference entities by identifier and never inline a name, so that the sensitive layer sits in one place, is versioned, and can be published on a different schedule from the counts.

label.description: Display name. In public examples, fixtures and test data this is always a fictional label such as 'Candidate A'. Real names appear only in a deployed, country-scoped registry, never in this repository.

isFictional.description: True for every entity in examples, tests and documentation. CI rejects fixtures where this is false.

aliases.description: Other written forms of the name actually encountered in sources: abbreviations, transliterations, misspellings that recur, and the local-language form. An alias list is not decoration: it is the join key of the whole system, and a missing alias shows up downstream as an actor who spent nothing.

electionRefs.description: Elections this entity takes part in, referencing the country configuration.

relations.description: Structural links to other entities. Kept explicit because spending routed through a coalition member or a friendly third party is the normal case, not the exception.

declaredFinance.description: What this entity officially declared, where a disclosure regime exists. This is the counterpart the estimate is compared against, and its absence is itself a finding.

matching.description: How raw strings from collectors resolve to this entity. Kept on the entity rather than in collector code so that a resolution rule is versioned, sourced and reviewable like any other record. Rules are applied after the normalisation described in ALIASES.md.

patterns.description: Regular expressions matched against a normalised candidate string. Anchored by the resolver; write them without anchors.

platformHandles.description: Account identifiers this entity controls on a platform. A handle is evidence of control and needs the same provenance as any other claim.

disclaimerStrings.description: Paid-for-by strings as they appear in ad libraries. These are the strongest attribution basis available for digital ads and the reason platform_declared outranks contextual inference.

doNotMatch.description: Strings that look like this entity and are not. A known-confusion list is how a resolver stops making the same wrong join every week.

minimumScore.description: Fuzzy-match threshold below which a candidate is queued for human review rather than joined. Defaults to the country configuration.
